text.p: Cleanup continues along the Red River in the upper Plains of the USA and in southern Manitoba, Canada, near Winnepeg. The next chance for moderate rain in the area does not come until late in the week. Rainfall so far this month has averaged below normal.

Tropical cyclone 36s (Rhonda) is becoming less of a threat to shipping in the southeast Indian Ocean as it weakens rapidly. It is expected to dissipate before it reaches the West Australia coast in less than 24 hours. It could still, however, cause locally strong winds and locally heavy rains as it moves inland.

Tropical Cyclone 01B is becoming an increasing risk to shipping as it strengthens and slowly moves northward in the Bay of Bengal. Top winds are currently 60 mph. Slow intensification is forecast over the next 24 hours. The system is still days away from threatening Bangladesh or Burma and is primarily a threat to shipping at this time.
